messages:
From: AJ Ramos <aj.ramos@digiscribe.com>

Cc: sara.patel@digiscribe.com, cto@digiscribe.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:58:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after variant shift (impacting 3% of traffic)

Hi Vivek,

We saw a sharp jump in p95 and p99 latencies starting ~10:43am PT coincident with the traffic shift to the new model variant you rolled for us as part of the A/B. Error rates also ticked up (5xxs from 0.2% -> 1.8%). This is impacting ingestion throughput for our summarization pipeline; queues are backing up.

Attached are the plots and a few trace snippets. Can you confirm whether the variant uses the new attention kernel you mentioned and whether there was any change to batching/timeout behavior?

This is causing rate-limiting downstream — we need immediate guidance on rollback or mitigation.

--
AJ Ramos
SRE, DigiScribe
aj.ramos@digiscribe.com

Vivek

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after variant shift (impacting 3% of traffic)

On it. Quick checks I ran against our canary logs: the new variant (v2027-11-02a) switches to the optimized grouped-attn kernel which should reduce latency for long context, but it also changes the KV cache alignment for sharded runtimes.

Prelim observations:
- At 10:42:43 PT we saw steady CPU/GPU utilisation but an uptick in tail scheduling latencies on nodes serving the branch.
- The traces AJ attached show repeated requeueing at the batching layer (requests waiting ~120ms extra in batch queues).

I recommend the following immediate steps:
1) Roll traffic for DigiScribe back to baseline model (v2027-10-18b) — this will remove the grouped-attn path and should restore tail.
2) Keep the variant disabled for regional pools until we can reproduce in staging with DigiScribe-like seq lengths.

If you approve, I'll trigger the rollback and monitor p95/p99 closely. We should also snapshot the failing nodes' kernel configs and core dumps for postmortem.

-Marcus
Senior Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after variant shift (impacting 3% of traffic)

Update: We rolled DigiScribe back to baseline variant at 14:02 PT (traffic routing change completed at 14:03 PT). Immediate monitoring shows p95 returning to normal within one minute; p99 trending down from the peak. 5xx rates dropped back to baseline.

Actions taken:
- Rollback to v2027-10-18b
- Isolated 6 nodes that reported batch queue requeues and captured kernel configs + heap snapshots (archived in incident bundle).
- Opened a staging reproduce with DigiScribe's token distribution.

Next steps: Marcus to lead deep-dive on KV cache alignment and batching heuristics; Product/Customer to determine acceptable reintroduction criteria.

Hannah
Director, Technical Support
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after variant shift (impacting 3% of traffic)

Sara / AJ — thank you for the quick coordination and for the traces. Summary for your execs and ours:

What happened:
- A variant with grouped-attn kernel was rolled to 3% of DigiScribe traffic at 10:43 PT.
- Variant introduced a KV cache alignment mismatch on sharded serving nodes which increased batching queue wait times and caused p95/p99 spikes and a small rise in 5xxs.

What we did:
- Immediate rollback at 14:02 PT; p95/p99 and 5xxs returned to baseline within ~60–90s.
- Captured node snapshots and traces; staging reproduce in progress.

Impact:
- Customer-visible latency spike affecting tail (p95/p99), temporary throughput degradation and queueing; no data loss.

Next steps / asks:
- Marcus will run a targeted reproduce with DigiScribe's token profiles and provide a mitigation plan (timeline EOD tomorrow).
- Product (Lauren) and DigiScribe will agree on acceptance criteria before reintroducing the variant (e.g., canary sequence, ramp thresholds, automated rollback).
- We'll prepare a short postmortem and a proposed credit/SLR adjustment for the window impacted (Vivek to coordinate commercial response).

I'll be available for a 30-min bridge if you want real-time updates. Apologies for the disruption — we'll own remediation.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
phone: +1-415-555-0199
